items.evidence: The reload step reads the note back from a freshly loaded page (diff lines 120-123, spec lines 49-52), so it would fail if the mutation never ran.
Actor `customer` (MANAGE_USERS only) is set at diff line 85. The note value after saving is asserted at diff line 116 and after a reload at diff line 123.

No existing page object covers the customer details screen. `findCustomerId` is a new lookup modelled on `findOrderId`, not a copy of it, and `CUSTOMER`/`ORDERS_SCENARIO` are reused from the scenario file.
No `waitForTimeout`, sleeps or fixed-delay polling. The waits are on element visibility and on the Save button's disabled state.
Imports `test`/`expect` from `fixtures/test.ts`, is not tagged `parallel()`, and does not write to the cache or the dumps.
Uses `data-test-id`s and a role locator for the Notifications region. `button-bar-confirm` is the single save-bar button, used the same way in `OrderPage`/`DraftOrderPage`.
Uses the orders scenario's existing customer. The only GraphQL call is a read-only id lookup.
The id is looked up by email at test time. Assertions use `CUSTOMER` constants and the test's own note text.
Uses the stored session of the `customer` actor (user.manager, MANAGE_USERS) through `test.use`. No UI sign-in and no credentials in the spec.
`typecheck.txt` reports exit 0 with no errors, and the spec is in `e2e/tests/customers/`.

`e2e/tests/customers/customer-note.spec.ts` (diff lines 102-106 and 115) builds locators inline in the spec (`customerPage.contactCard.getByTestId("customer-email")`, `"customer-first-name"`, `notifications.getByText("Customer updated")`) instead of defining them as fields on `CustomerPage`.
`CustomerPage` uses `readonly` fields initialised from `this.page` and `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`.
Has `// Arrange` and `// Act & Assert` comments, the suite's pattern for interleaved stages.
One test for the one story, with a `test.step` for each stage (open, write and save, reload).
The title describes the behaviour and carries `#e2e` plus an area tag.
The header comment (diff lines 78-84) says what the spec covers, why it uses the `customer` actor, and why it reloads.
All assertions are web-first (`toHaveValue`, `toBeVisible`, `toBeDisabled`, `toHaveURL`).
Uses `ORDERS_SCENARIO`, `CUSTOMER.email` and `CUSTOMER.firstName`. The note literal is the test's own input.
No cleanup hooks and no unique or timestamped names.
No `timeout` or `retries` overrides, no `networkidle`, no `waitForLoadState`.

Relative imports keep the `.ts` extension. The page object imports `expect` from `@playwright/test`, as `homePage.ts` and `draftOrderPage.ts` already do. The spec takes `test` and `expect` from the fixture only.
`gql` is typed (`gql<{ user: { id: string } | null }>`), with no `any` and no casts.
The comments explain reasons (why `save()` waits for the disabled state, why a clean form after reload shows the value came from the server). None just restate the next line.

structured_output.summary: A solid submission: 22 of the 23 items are met, and the only failure is the minor M1. It runs as the single-permission `customer` actor on the orders scenario, finds Ada Lovelace by email instead of a hard-coded id, and proves the note was saved by reading it back after a reload. It type-checks. The spec builds some locators inline (the email and first-name fields, and the "Customer updated" toast) instead of putting them on `CustomerPage`. The diff also adds a planning file, `specs/customer-note.md`, which no checklist item covers.
